prompt: Evaluate $\arcsin\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$. Give your answer in degrees, as a number only.
hint: Read it as a question: "which angle has a sine of $\frac{1}{2}$?"

hints.text: Read it as a question: "which angle has a sine of $\frac{1}{2}$?"
Think of your special triangles — one of the famous angles has sine exactly $\frac{1}{2}$.

explanation: $\arcsin$ undoes $\sin$: it takes a ratio and hands back the angle.
We need the angle whose sine is $\frac{1}{2}$, and $\sin 30^\circ = \frac{1}{2}$.

alternativeExplanations.title: From the 30-60-90 triangle
steps: In a $30$-$60$-$90$ triangle the side opposite the $30^\circ$ angle is exactly half the hypotenuse.
That is precisely the statement $\sin 30^\circ = \frac{1}{2}$, read backwards.
